pt-PT.question: Nos mercados astecas, que sementes eram usadas como moeda?
pt-PT.explanation: Sementes de cacau: segundo o arqueólogo Michael E. Smith, pagavam as compras do dia a dia, enquanto os tecidos de algodão serviam para os bens mais valiosos. O cacau era também a bebida da elite e um tributo exigido à região de Soconusco.

en-US.question: In Aztec markets, which seeds were used as currency?
en-US.explanation: Cacao seeds: according to archaeologist Michael E. Smith, they paid for everyday purchases, while cotton cloth was used for more valuable goods. Cacao was also the elite's drink and a tribute demanded from the Soconusco region.

fontes.titulo: When Money Grew on Trees | CHOCOLATE: Food of the Gods (Cornell University Library)
fontes.excerto: This facsimile from the Codex Mendoza (c. 1541) shows tribute that the Aztecs extracted twice a year from the cacao-growing region of Soconusco in southern Mexico. Next to the jaguar skins are two loads of cacao beans, which were used as currency as well as the drink of the elite.

fontes.titulo: ASU archaeologist talks Aztec currency with New York Times | ASU News
fontes.excerto: Smith notes that ancient Mesoamerican currency was chiefly cacao for day-to-day items and cotton cloth for more valuable goods. "If you wanted to buy a taco at the marketplace, you'd use cacao beans," says Smith
most of us know that they used cacao (cocoa) beans as a simple rate of exchange... cocoa beans generally formed 'the every day small change'; one small rabbit = 30, one turkey egg = 3

verificador.notas: Mercado de Tlatelolco e preços em cacau (Frances Berdan, citando Bray e o Códice Florentino). 2.ª fonte lida: Lam Museum of Anthropology (Wake Forest University): 'People used cacao beans as money'. Feijões, milho e abóbora não aparecem como moeda.

advogado.notas: Cornell e ASU nível 1; Mexicolore nível 2; Infopédia 403.

editor.notas: explicação encurtada para 1–2 frases (migração v2); sem factos novos

tradutor.notas: Attribution to Michael E. Smith kept. 'Cacao' (not 'cocoa') as in the sources.

historico.nota: Clássico de dificuldade 2 fixado pelo Andre. Enunciado diferente da 000011 (sem tributos). Explicação separa moeda de mercado (Smith/ASU) e tributo de Soconusco (Codex Mendoza/Cornell). Números de uma só fonte excluídos. Distratores por exclusão; amaranto evitado. Fonte portuguesa de nível 1: Infopédia ($cacau) — 403.
